entries.name: Leonard Peltier

expected.sentence: Life sentence, commuted to home confinement. Released from federal prison February 18, 2025 to return to the Turtle Mountain reservation. Home confinement is distinct from an unconditional pardon or completed sentence. Source: https://ndncollective.org/leonard-peltier-released-from-49-years-of-wrongful-incarceration/

updates.sentence: Life sentence, commuted to home confinement. Released from federal prison February 18, 2025 to return to the Turtle Mountain reservation. Home confinement is distinct from an unconditional pardon or completed sentence. Source: https://ndncollective.org/leonard-peltier-released-from-49-years-of-wrongful-incarceration/ U.S. custody began with his extradition from Canada on December 18, 1976. The recorded U.S. custody periods exclude his escape from July 20 to July 25, 1979; his earlier Canadian detention is not included in those periods.

entries.rationale: Peltier own 1979 statement printed p26 explicitly dates extradition December 18, 1976, independently corroborated in Amnesty 1977 report. Breakthrough Winter 1980 printed p23 dates escape July 20, 1979 and recapture five days later; contemporaneous Militant August 10, 1979 p29 explicitly dates recapture July 25. All three local originals visually checked. Preserve verified Canadian arrest and existing 2025 prison-release endpoint, exclude escape interval.

entries.name: Anna Mae Pictou Aquash

expected.convicted: Held in pretrial federal custody before release on bond; never tried
expected.sentence:
Several days at Pennington County Jail on the September 1975 charges; further brief custody after the November 1975 Oregon arrest; killed shortly after her second release in unresolved circumstances on or about December 12, 1975

Charges as recorded: Weapons and explosives charges arising from the September 5, 1975 federal raid on the AIM property at Pine Ridge; later additional charges in Oregon

entries.rationale: Inquiry Concerning Indian Matters, FBI statement printed p278 (PDF145), identifies Aquash as arrested at the September 5, 1975 search of Al Running residence, Grass Mountain, Rosebud Reservation. Correct one-day erroneous start; preserve existing separately established September 8 release and November case.

entries.name: Francis Mel Madden

expected.charges: Conspiracy and destruction of Selective Service records (the August 22, 1971 Camden, NJ draft-board raid).
expected.convicted: No — severed from the main trial; charges dismissed after the May 20, 1973 acquittals
expected.sentence: Never tried. Severed from the seventeen-defendant trial; the charges were dismissed after the jury acquitted all seventeen on May 20, 1973. About three weeks of pretrial custody in August-September 1971 under the collective bail strategy; individual release date unresolved.

updates.sentence: Never tried. Severed from the seventeen-defendant trial; the charges were dismissed after the jury acquitted all seventeen on May 20, 1973. Arrested August 22, 1971 and released the same day after a hearing before Magistrate Charles L. Rudd on a $5,000 own-recognizance bond.

entries.rationale: Individual FBI entry for Francis Mel Madden, PDF97 printed62, explicitly states apprehension August 22 and release on the same date. Existing exact date fields are correct; the incompatible three-week collective-custody narrative is not individually supported and is corrected.

entries.name: Darrelle Dean “Dino” Butler

expected.charges: Federal first-degree murder of FBI agents Jack Coler and Ronald Williams — June 26, 1975 firefight at the Jumping Bull compound, Pine Ridge Reservation
expected.sentence:
Held in pretrial detention 10 months; acquitted on self-defense grounds

Verdict as recorded: No — acquitted, U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Iowa, July 1976

updates.sentence: Held in pretrial detention in the FBI-agent murder prosecution and acquitted on self-defense grounds in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Iowa on July 16, 1976. The acquittal did not end his physical custody: contemporary reporting on July 19 stated that he returned to jail while serving a separate two-year sentence for possession of a firearm as a felon. His final physical release date is not established by these sources.

entries.rationale: Daily Iowan July 19 front-page reporter account explicitly says Butler and Robideau returned to jail after acquittal, Butler on separate firearms sentence. Militant July 30 p3 dates acquittal July 16. Existing July 15 endpoint predates acquittal and is not actual release; remove false endpoint rather than substitute acquittal date. Existing September arrest/incarceration remains pending verification.
